turns.content:
Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the complete Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Let me start with Phase 1 — all setup tasks in parallel.Colors and fonts are set. Now generating the logo and fetching all images in parallel.All assets ready. Now building the API, Header, and Footer in parallel.Now I'll build everything in parallel — the API endpoint, Header, Footer, and all three pages.Now register the API route and build all three pages simultaneously.Now register the API route and update routes.tsx with all three pages.Now let me verify the API endpoint works and check the RootLayout to make sure Header/Footer are wired up.API returns 200 with all 12 products. Header and Footer are already wired into RootLayout. Let me update the default meta description in RootLayout.Now mark all todo items complete.The full Artisan Goods Co. website is live. Here's what was built:

**Homepage** — Full-bleed hero with terracotta gradient overlay, animated headline, and dual CTAs. An asymmetric 4-card featured products grid (one 2× tall card) pulls live data from the API. A warm newsletter signup section with organic shape accents rounds it out.

**Product Catalog** (`/products`) — Products load via a React Router loader from `/api/products`. Sticky filter tabs (All | Pottery | Textiles | Woodwork | Jewelry) filter the 12 products client-side with animated transitions. Each card shows a square image, category badge, price, and an "Add to Cart" button.

**About Page** (`/about`) — Full-bleed hero, a 2-column founding story with values icons, a large centered mission pull-quote on forest green, and a 4-person team grid with circular photos and terracotta accent dots.

**Shared Header & Footer** — Sticky header with animated underline nav links, mobile hamburger menu, and the generated logo. Multi-column footer on deep forest green with social icons and a mini newsletter form.

**API** — `GET /api/products` returns 12 handmade products across all four categories, each with real product photography.

input.prompt:
Build a full multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.", a handmade crafts shop. All pages must be built and fully functional.

PROJECT DETAILS:
- Business: Artisan Goods Co. — handmade crafts shop
- Products: Pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry
- Audience: Craft lovers, gift shoppers, design-conscious consumers
- Tone: Warm, artisanal, authentic, premium-handmade

DESIGN DIRECTION:
Warm and earthy aesthetic that feels handcrafted and authentic — like a well-curated artisan market. Rich terracotta, warm cream, and deep forest green palette. Typography mixes a warm serif for headings with a clean sans-serif for body text. Layouts use generous whitespace, organic asymmetry, and full-bleed imagery sections to evoke the texture and warmth of handmade goods.

LAYOUT TYPE: Standard
Multi-page site with shared header navigation and footer.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
- Color: Warm earthy tones — terracotta (#C4622D), warm cream (#F5EFE0), deep forest green (#2D4A3E), soft sand (#E8D5B0). NOT generic white/gray.
- Typography: Warm serif for headings (Playfair Display or Lora), clean humanist sans for body (Source Sans Pro or Nunito). Generous line-height.
- Layout: Full-bleed hero with overlay text, asymmetric product grids, editorial section breaks. NO uniform icon grids.

VISUAL ELEMENTS:
- Primary: Photography (product shots, lifestyle, craft process)
- Style: Warm, natural lighting; textured backgrounds; handmade aesthetic
- Application: Hero full-bleed, product cards with square images, team photos circular
- Logo: Generate a logo using the media-logo skill — warm serif wordmark "Artisan Goods Co." with a small handcraft icon (e.g., a simple pottery vessel or leaf motif). Earthy terracotta/green palette.

MOTION DESIGN:
- Level: Subtle
- Effects: Fade-in on scroll for sections (400ms ease-out), hover lift on product cards (translateY -4px + shadow), smooth underline draw on nav links, gentle scale on CTA buttons
- Personality: Warm and unhurried — nothing snappy or corporate

SECTION-SPECIFIC:

Hero (Homepage):
- Full-bleed background image of handmade goods/workshop
- Overlaid headline: "Crafted with Care, Made to Last"
- Subheadline and two CTAs: "Shop Now" → /products, "Our Story" → /about
- Warm gradient overlay (terracotta to transparent)

Featured Products (Homepage):
- 4-card asymmetric grid (one card larger/featured)
- Each card: product image, name, category badge, price, hover reveal "View Product"
- "Browse All Products" link below

Newsletter Signup (Homepage):
- Full-width warm-toned section with organic shape accent
- Headline: "Join Our Craft Community"
- Email input + subscribe button
- Subtle background texture

PRODUCT CATALOG PAGE (/products):
- Page title + category filter tabs: All | Pottery | Textiles | Woodwork | Jewelry
- Products fetched from /api/products via React Router loader
- Responsive grid: 3 columns desktop, 2 tablet, 1 mobile
- Each product card: square image, category badge, name, price, "Add to Cart" button (non-functional, UI only)
- Filter tabs update displayed products client-side (filter the loaded data)
- Loading skeleton state while data loads

ABOUT PAGE (/about):
- Hero section: full-width image with "Our Story" heading
- Brand story section: 2-column layout (text left, image right) — founding story, values
- Mission statement: large pull-quote style, centered, terracotta accent
- Team section: grid of 3-4 team member cards — circular photo, name, role, short bio
- Closing CTA linking to /products

SHARED HEADER (src/layouts/parts/Header.tsx):
- Style: Professional with artisan warmth
- Logo left, nav links center/right: Home | Products | About
- Warm cream background, terracotta accent on active/hover
- Mobile hamburger menu
- Sticky on scroll with subtle shadow

SHARED FOOTER (src/layouts/parts/Footer.tsx):
- Style: Multi-column
- Columns: Brand blurb + social icons | Quick Links | Categories | Newsletter mini-form
- Warm dark background (deep forest green or near-black)
- Light cream text

DIFFERENTIATION: Asymmetric featured product grid on homepage where one card is 2x size. Full-bleed earthy photography throughout. Warm serif headings create editorial feel unlike generic e-commerce templates.

CONSISTENCY: Maintain earthy warmth throughout — footer as intentional as hero. Terracotta accents used consistently as the action/highlight color.

BUILD ORDER:

Phase 1 — Setup (run in parallel):
- Search for images: artisan workshop hero, pottery products, textile products, woodwork products, jewelry products, team member portraits, about page hero
- Set font stack using fontTheme tool: Playfair Display (headings) + Source Sans Pro or Nunito (body)
- Set color scheme using colorTheme tool: terracotta primary, warm cream background, forest green secondary
- Generate logo using media-logo skill

Phase 2 — API + Structure (run in parallel after Phase 1):
- Build /api/products Express endpoint in src/server/api/products.ts — return 12 mock products across 4 categories (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) each with: id, name, category, price, description, imageUrl (use fetched Getty image URLs)
- Register the API handler in src/server/entry.ts
- Build Header (src/layouts/parts/Header.tsx) — sticky, warm cream, logo + nav + mobile menu
- Build Footer (src/layouts/parts/Footer.tsx) — multi-column, forest green dark background

Phase 3 — Pages (after Phase 1 & 2):
- Build Homepage (src/pages/index.tsx): hero, featured products (fetch from /api/products, show first 4), newsletter signup
- Add route loader to routes.tsx for /products that fetches from /api/products
- Build Product Catalog (src/pages/products.tsx): filter tabs, product grid, loading states
- Build About page (src/pages/about.tsx): story, mission, team grid

Phase 4 — Routes + Finalize:
- Update src/routes.tsx to include all three routes: /, /products, /about — with loader on /products
- Mark all todo items as COMPLETE using the todoList tool
- Show the finished site

ROUTES (src/routes.tsx):
```tsx
[
  { path: '/', element: <HomePage /> },
  {
    path: '/products',
    element: <ProductsPage />,
    loader: async () => {
      const res = await fetch('/api/products');
      return { products: await res.json() };
    }
  },
  { path: '/about', element: <AboutPage /> }
]
```

API SHAPE (/api/products response):
```json
[
  {
    "id": "1",
    "name": "Hand-Thrown Terracotta Bowl",
    "category": "pottery",
    "price": 48,
    "description": "Wheel-thrown stoneware with a warm terracotta glaze.",
    "imageUrl": "<getty image url>"
  }
]
```

TODO LIST MANAGEMENT:
After completing all pages and the API, mark ALL todo items as complete using the todoList tool:
- Homepage
- Product catalog page
- About page
- Shared navigation & footer
- Products API endpoint

INITIAL SCOPE: Build ALL pages as requested — this is a full multi-page site build, not just a homepage preview.

How It Began

Born from a love of things made by hand

Artisan Goods Co. was founded in 2014 when Sarah Chen, a ceramicist working out of her garage studio, realized she wasn't alone in her frustration with a world flooded with disposable, mass-produced goods.

She began connecting with other local makers — woodworkers, weavers, jewelers — and together they started selling at farmers markets and pop-up events. The response was overwhelming. People were hungry for things made with care.

turns.content: Can you make sure the header and footer show up consistently on every page through a shared layout component? I want to confirm that all three pages — home, products, and about — are all wrapped in the same layout, not each managing their own header and footer separately.

Good news — this is already set up correctly. Let me show you exactly how it works.Everything is already wired up exactly as you'd want. Here's the full picture:

**`RootLayout.tsx`** is the single shared layout — it renders `<Header />`, then `{children}`, then `<Footer />`. Neither Header nor Footer appears anywhere in the individual page files.

**`App.tsx`** wraps the entire route tree in one `<RootLayout><Outlet /></RootLayout>`. The `<Outlet />` is where React Router swaps in whichever page matches the current URL — `/`, `/products`, or `/about`. The layout itself never unmounts during navigation, so the header and footer stay mounted and consistent across all three pages.

No page manages its own header or footer. If you ever need to change the nav links, footer copy, or layout structure, `Header.tsx`, `Footer.tsx`, and `RootLayout.tsx` are the only files you'd touch — and the change applies everywhere automatically.
